reading.body:
AI risk is being repriced and moved out of standard insurance into captives, mutual pools, surplus lines, and capital markets, with coverage tied directly to compute availability and model performance.

The pattern is substitution. Where traditional carriers decline risk, hyperscalers form single parent captives to self-insure, startups pool catastrophic legal costs, and complex AI liability migrates to surplus lines and Lloyds. Parametric micro-insurance pays out on API and GPU availability, and catastrophe bonds hedge multi-day cloud outages, so compute uptime becomes an insurable event rather than an assumed operating condition.

For AI specifically, this means insurance is starting to track the two things that determine whether models can run at all: compute access and output reliability. Insured performance guarantees back vendor commitments on model output, while certification-linked discounts reward enterprises that pass third party safety audits. Generative AI exclusion endorsements remove that risk from general liability cover, and reinsurance capacity caps limit the maximum cover available to operators.

What the data does not show is scale or price. It lists ten mechanisms but gives no premiums, loss ratios, claim volumes, or binding capacity figures. It also says nothing about physical power or building risk, which are not among these instruments.
